article_title: The Effect of Phonetic Transcription on Iranian EFL Students' Word Stress Learning
citation: Ghorbani, M. R. (2019). The effect of phonetic transcription on Iranian EFL students' word stress learning. Journal of Language and Linguistic Studies, 15(2), 400-410. https://www.jlls.org
title: 60-item word stress identification test based on The Flatmates episodes
description: The researcher developed a 60-item achievement pre-test from words taken from the CD scripts of 20 lessons of The Flatmates series from the BBC's learning English website. Items included 20 two-syllable, 20 three-syllable, and 20 four-syllable words; subjects put a check mark on the syllable receiving primary stress, each item weighted one point. "Based on Kuder-Richardson Formula 21, the reliability of the test was 0.71." The test was re-administered as the post-test after a six-week interval.
requirements: Piloting with students and KR-21 reliability checking before use
constraints: The sample of words was not randomly spaced across lesson scripts
Assessment was written only, not oral
target_learning_goals: Identifying the syllable carrying primary stress in English words
examples: Used as pre-test and, rearranged after six weeks, as post-test for both groups
key_sources: Ghorbani, M. R. (2019). The effect of phonetic transcription on Iranian EFL students' word stress learning. Journal of Language and Linguistic Studies, 15(2), 400-410. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=EJ1220802

article_title: A Comparative Study of Testing Grammar Knowledge of Iranian Students between Cloze and Multiple-Choice Tests
citation: Minoo Alemi & Apama Miraghaee. (2011). A Comparative Study of Testing Grammar Knowledge of Iranian Students between Cloze and Multiple-Choice Tests. i-manager's Journal of English Language Teaching, Vol. 1, No. 3, July - September 2011. https://www.i-manager.com
title: 60-item grammar post-test combining a 30-blank cloze passage and 30 multiple-choice items
description: The study's outcome measure was a 60-item achievement test of grammar with two parts: a cloze passage with 30 blanks followed by its 30 multiple-choice answers, and a 30-item multiple-choice grammar section. Students had 80 minutes to mark answers. Its reliability was checked by KR-21 in a pilot study and its validity by correlating with a Nelson test, yielding a reliability of 0.94 and a validity correlation of 0.41.
requirements: Validated through a pilot study with 31 freshman Iranian EFL students and correlational procedures
constraints: Validity correlation of 0.41 was characterized by the article as only a moderate relationship
examples: Seven items (items 21, 22, 28, 30, 31, 46, and 47) were deleted from the Nelson test to give it pure grammatical content
